item.description:
The first release of Silica, a lightweight code editor for macOS, made of glass.
### What's in it
- **Projects.** Open a folder to get a window with a file tree that follows changes on disk and dims what your `.gitignore` excludes. Create, rename and trash files right in the tree, and filter it as you type. - **Quick Open (⌘P)** with fuzzy matching, and **Find in Project (⇧⌘F)**. - **Syntax highlighting** for 25 languages, including Swift, JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Go, Rust, C, C++ and Markdown. - **Nine color themes**, each with a light and a dark palette: Atom One, GitHub, Xcode, Solarized, Catppuccin, Gruvbox, Tokyo Night, Rosé Pine and Dracula. - **Markdown preview (⇧⌘V)**, with highlighted code blocks. - **Editing tools**: tabs, line numbers, indent guides, a minimap, word wrap, Go to Line (⌘L), toggle comment (⌘/), and moving or duplicating lines (⌥↑ ⌥↓). - Projects **reopen their tabs** where you left them, and recent projects are on the welcome window. - **Open With** in Finder, the Dock icon and `open -a Silica` all open files and folders in Silica.
### Installing
Open the DMG and drag Silica to Applications. Silica needs macOS 27 or later.
From now on, Silica checks for updates once a day and installs them for you. You can also use **Silica › Check for Updates…**, or turn automatic checks off in Settings › General.
### Feedback
This is an early release, so expect some rough edges. If you find a bug or have an idea, please [open an issue](https://github.com/dqhieu/Silica/issues).
